title: Anthropic's Public Benefit Charter
content:
Our charter is to responsibly develop and maintain advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity.
Anthropic is a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC), a designation that requires us to balance the financial interests of shareholders with the benefit to the broader public. Our Public Benefit Report takes stock of what we are doing to serve the public benefit, and of the work ahead.
Read our 2026 Public Benefit Report
- The technical problems of AI safety are solved.Powerful AI can be developed and deployed without severe, irreversible harms.
- AI safety is a universal practice backstopped by law.AI developers everywhere follow safe development and deployment practices, sustained by industry norms and enforced by regulation.
- AI strengthens democracy and global stability.Democracies hold the lead in AI and use it to better serve the public and promote peace.
- AI expands prosperity and human flourishing.AI enables unprecedented economic growth, and the resulting prosperity empowers every person to pursue a good life.
- AI’s benefits are shared by everyone.AI delivers transformative benefits that reach people everywhere, and the opportunities AI creates are distributed.
Explore the work
Learn more about our research, policies, and programs. We plan to add to this record over time.

report.summary: Anthropic reaffirms its Public Benefit Corporation status and publishes a 2026 report outlining five long-term goals for safe, beneficial AI.
report.background: Anthropic was founded in 2021 as a Public Benefit Corporation, a US legal structure that obliges directors to weigh a stated public mission alongside shareholder returns rather than profit alone. That structure has become a distinguishing feature as AI labs face mounting scrutiny over safety, concentration of power and societal disruption. Rival labs have also restructured around public-benefit frameworks, and governments are drafting AI laws that could harden voluntary commitments into regulation. Charters like this one are partly a governance instrument, partly a trust signal to policymakers, customers and researchers weighing whether frontier labs can police themselves. Critics note that such documents are self-imposed and largely unenforceable without external oversight, while supporters argue they create accountability through public reporting and internal mandate.
key_points: Legal commitment, not just branding: as a PBC, Anthropic must balance shareholder financial interests against a chartered public benefit and report on progress, which constrains purely commercial decisions in principle.

Five stated end goals: the charter frames success as solved AI safety, safety practices universal and backed by law, democracies leading in AI, broad economic prosperity, and benefits distributed across the population rather than captured by a few.
The 2026 Public Benefit Report is the accountability mechanism: it takes stock of research, policy and programs to date and is described as a record that will be expanded over time.
Safety as a legal floor, not a promise: the charter explicitly imagines industry norms eventually enforced by regulation, an implicit acknowledgement that voluntary practice alone is insufficient.

Governance and politics bundled together: the document ties technical safety work to democratic stability and shared prosperity, positioning AI development as a civic issue rather than a purely engineering one.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the charter adds pressure on rival labs to publish comparable commitments and metrics, nudging governance toward structured public reporting rather than one-off safety pledges. For developers, it signals that model access, usage policies and safety evaluations may keep shifting as the company aligns products with stated goals, and that interpretability and evaluation work will remain priorities. For regular users, the practical effect is indirect: the charter shapes how products are released, restricted and audited, but it does not by itself guarantee outcomes. The real test is whether future reports disclose measurable progress and failures, since a charter whose goals are broad enough cannot be falsified offers limited accountability.
report.tools: To follow the substance rather than the framing, read Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy and AI Safety Level thresholds, which translate safety goals into concrete deployment gates. Pair that with Inspect, the UK AI Safety Institute's open-source evaluation framework, for hands-on model testing, and with published interpretability work such as the Transformer Circuits research threads. Developers can also track Claude's API documentation and usage policies to see how governance commitments surface in product behaviour.
